mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during periods of rising FEDFUNDS above 4%, or the S&P 500 closes lower in the subsequent 20 days despite the rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as higher unemployment is associated with weaker equity risk sentiment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 6.5%, or the unemployment rate shows no correlation with SPX returns over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 102.0, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive due to expectations of stronger economic momentum and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: No significant relationship between INDPRO > 102.0 and positive 20-day SPX returns across multiple backtests, or the IC is below 0.05 in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly GDP deflator (implied by CPIAUCSL < 236.0) for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals soft inflation, prompting rate cut expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL remains below 236.0 for two months, or the inflation surprise is positive and SPX outperforms.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (industrial production) over the prior month produce a statistically significant positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return through risk-off arbitrage in equity futures.
regime_hint: Dual softening in rates and industrial activity
failure_condition: No significant interaction effect detected (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests, or 20-day returns are not positive when both proxies move in the same direction contrary to expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in PAYEMS (employment) above 138,000 triggers a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as labor market strength supports optimism about corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when PAYEMS crosses above 138,000, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is negative due to reduced consumer demand expectations and tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < previous month's value for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when RSAFS shows this downward trend, or the effect is spurious (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for four consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive due to expectations of future rate cuts and easing credit constraints.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive in this regime, or the effect is not robust across multiple regime shifts (p > 0.05).
